Done. The full suite is green (6 tests, 0 failures).

## What I changed

The business-day rule already rolled weekends forward but ignored public holidays. I extended it in the one place that owns the definition of "business day."

**`BusinessDays.java`** (`rest/function/owner/`) — added the fixed holiday calendar and made the roll-forward skip holidays as well as weekends:
- New `PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` constant: `2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28`.
- Extracted a single `isBusinessDay(date)` predicate (not Sat, not Sun, not a holiday) and rewrote `rollForward` to advance one day until it hits a business day. This naturally chains past runs of weekend + holiday.

The pipeline (`RollRegistrationDateToBusinessDay`, `EnsureDailyLimit`, and `owners.POST.yml`) needed no changes — they already delegate to `BusinessDays.rollForward`, so both the new-owner default date and the daily-limit count now respect holidays automatically.

**`BusinessDaysTest.java`** (new unit test, same package to reach the package-private helper) covers:
- plain weekday unchanged,
- weekend → Monday,
- weekday holidays (Thu 01-01 → Fri 01-02; Mon 01-26 → Tue 01-27),
- a holiday that also falls on a weekend (Sat 04-25 → Mon 04-27),
- the consecutive-obstacle chain (Fri 12-25 holiday → weekend → Mon 12-28 holiday → Tue 12-29).

The existing `AcceptanceTest` (weekend invariant on the default date) still passes.
